class.name: NetwDisplayChannel
class.brief_description: One independently smoothed value stream: where it is sampled, how it is smoothed, and where it is written.
class.description: A display runtime holds one of these per channel. The channel carries the whole path a value takes: [member source_obj] and [member source_prop] name where it is sampled, [member spec] and [member history] decide what is shown for a given playhead, [member offset] holds whatever residual is gliding off, and [member output] writes it. Both object ends are held by instance id and resolved at each read, so a freed node answers [code]null[/code] rather than a pointer nobody may follow. That is why they are read through the properties rather than cached by a caller. [codeblock] var channel := NetwDisplayChannel.new() channel.name = &"position" channel.state_key = &"%d/position" % body.get_instance_id() channel.spec = interpolate channel.history = NetwDisplayHistory.new() channel.source_obj = body channel.source_prop = &"position" channel.target_prop = &"position" [/codeblock] A channel has two names for two questions, exactly as [NetwDisplayTracks] indexes them: [member state_key] is its identity, the object and property it samples, and [member name] is what a caller addresses it by, the property it writes.

method.name: copy_shape_from
method.description: Adopts [param other]'s SHAPE: its spec, its two object ends, its two property names and its self-feedback verdict. This is what a re-declaration does to a channel that already exists, so the identity, the recorded history, the writer, the offset and the last written value all stay. [member authoring_ticks] is the one field that accumulates rather than replaces: a channel that has ever carried the authoring stream still carries it, because a second declaration that happens not to author does not un-author the first. A null [param other] changes nothing, because a channel with no twin is already its own shape.

method.name: snap
method.description: Writes [param value] out immediately and forgets everything that would have smoothed away from it: the recorded samples, the held render offset, and the value the next pass would have eased from. This is what a teleport is. A snap that kept the history would glide back toward the pose it just left.

members.member: Whether this channel's samples carry the authoring tick stamp, which is what the displayed tick is read from.
The recorded samples this channel is displayed from.
The value last written through [member output], which the next pass smooths away from and holds when the history has nothing newer.
The property this channel writes, which is what a caller addresses it by.
The render offset holding the visual still through a correction or a change of display source. Minted with the channel, so no caller has to remember to.
The writer one smoothed value is handed to. Swappable: a test backend records the sequence instead of touching a node.

[code]true[/code] when the channel writes the very property it samples on the very object it samples it from. A remote display writes it harmlessly because the body is frozen; a predicted or authority pump skips it, because feeding a display filter into the simulation it is filtering is a drag with no bottom.
The object this channel samples, or [code]null[/code] once it has been freed.
The property sampled on [member source_obj]. Empty for a channel with no source at all, which is what an event argument is.
How this channel is smoothed, and what it does past its newest sample.
The channel's identity, the object and property it samples. Two declarations of one key describe one channel twice.
The object this channel writes, or [code]null[/code] once it has been freed. The same object as [member source_obj] unless a visual root or a redirect took the write elsewhere.
